finding.summary: New design-doc bullet overstates the behaviour: "A dry run never reaches the network" is now a universal claim, but many read commands still fetch under --dry-run
finding.evidence: The added bullet reads: "Reads honour the flag too: `docs list`, `docs get`, `sheets tabs list`, and `sheets cells get` print their GET without fetching. A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." The second sentence is a blanket guarantee, yet in the same tree `notes list` (packages/cli/src/commands/notes.ts:35), `notes get` (:76), `slides list`/`slides get` (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:35,76), `files list`/`files get` (packages/cli/src/commands/files.ts:85,105), `sheets export` (packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:39) and `api-keys list` (packages/cli/src/commands/api-keys.ts:31) all issue the request regardless of `opts.dryRun`. A design doc that promises an invariant the implementation only partially satisfies is worse than an enumerated list; either scope the sentence to the four commands or cover the rest.

verdict.reason: The quoted bullet exists verbatim at docs/design/cli.md:824-827, including the universal claim "A dry run never reaches the network, so it burns no rate limit and emits no access log even when the command is harmless." Dry-run handling is per-command, not centralized: packages/cli/src/client/dry-run.ts only prints a request, and packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts contains no dryRun handling at all, so there is no guard making the claim true. Multiple read commands issue their request without consulting opts.dryRun: notes list (commands/notes.ts:35) and notes get (:76), slides list (commands/slides.ts:40) and slides get (:81), files list (commands/files.ts:85) and files get (:105), sheets export (commands/sheets-export.ts:39), and api-keys list (commands/api-keys.ts:31 — that file imports no dry-run helper at all). Write paths in the same files do gate on opts.dryRun (e.g. notes.ts:55, 89, 107), confirming the pattern is opt-in per command. The design doc therefore asserts an invariant the implementation only partially satisfies, which is a design-doc/spec-conformance fit violation in this lens's lane (not a line-level logic, security, or test-quality issue). No refutation ground applies.
